Definition: a master; hence, a husband, or (figuratively) owner (often used with another noun in modifications of this latter sense)
BiblicalUsage: Baal as a common word means a master, a husband, an owner — the one who has the right to a thing. A married woman has a baal, a man is the baal of his house and his goods, the owner of the ox is its baal, and the master of the dream is the man who holds it. The same word names the lord of the house and, in the next entry, the false god who claimed to be lord of all.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the word itself is not the problem — a husband is a baal, and that is right and good. The problem is when men give the title to a god of wood and stone, and I believe God is the only true Baal, the only true Master, of his people.
